findings.title: Keep concrete assembly and concrete type dispatch under review
findings.detail: For concern 1, O4 can close a static acquisition rule over declared implementation symbols, import statements and a restricted export grammar. O5 closes the raw registry route within its own boundary. Neither covers selection among injected factories, even when the consumer sees only interfaces. I appended a `cfg.name` branch that selected and called one of two passed factories to `training/cv_trainer.py` in memory. The real R0–R5 checker accepted it. The direct Config import negative controls cover a narrower property, and Config union validation is explicitly allowed. For concern 2, O4 can deny a direct import of a protected result or implementation class. An import-free branch on `type(x).__name__ == 'CalibrationResult'` also passed the checker. Nominal checks, class patterns, type-keyed tables, strings, derived values and objects already in hand do not form a closed grammar for either semantic concern. Enumerating their spellings would reopen R6. Keep both concerns under review, including computed `getattr`, `eval`/`exec`, `type(obj)(...)`, reflection on injected objects and runtime monkey-patching. Evidence at tests/test_architecture/test_layer_rules.py:131, tests/test_architecture/_layer_rules.py:355 and HISTORY.md:14143.

findings.title: If O4 is adopted, forbid access through re-exporting namespaces at the import boundary
findings.detail: Choose import restrictions over following arbitrary Python re-exports. `resolve` returns `lizyml.metrics` for `from lizyml.metrics import RMSE` and for `*`, and records only a module edge for `import lizyml.metrics as m`. In an estimator module, all three forms passed R0–R5, as did the unaliased dotted import, `from lizyml import metrics as m`, and a direct import of `metrics.regression`. The estimator-to-metrics allowance is category-wide. A Layer 2 named import from the metrics package already fails R3, but `from lizyml.metrics.registry import lizyml as pkg` passed and supplies a root namespace from which `pkg.metrics.RMSE` can be reached. An O4 rule must inspect the original imported name and the binding produced. Require non-owners to use explicit named imports from an allowlist of safe bindings. Reject star imports and namespace bindings that expose a protected name or a path to one, including implicit parent bindings from unaliased dotted imports, `from parent import child`, and aliases of those namespaces. Preserve public package exports for callers outside `lizyml`. For producers, restrict re-exports to declared, statically named bindings with known sources, including aliases and finite chains. Reject undeclared carriers and unsupported export forms in the checked surface, including producer stars, computed exports and module `__getattr__`. A package-only denylist leaves ordinary modules and IF modules available as intermediate carriers. This closes the restricted import and export grammar. Values returned by calls, runtime imports and namespaces obtained by reflection remain outside it. Evidence at tests/test_architecture/_layer_rules.py:291, tests/test_architecture/test_layer_rules.py:417, lizyml/metrics/registry.py:11, lizyml/metrics/__init__.py:24, lizyml/estimators/__init__.py:4 and lizyml/estimators/lgbm/__init__.py:7.

findings.title: Treat 1-C as an explicit internal import contract
findings.detail: `__all__` controls star imports. Explicit `from module import name` and `module.name` can still access a bound name omitted from it. The metrics IF currently binds `MetricRegistry` and the `lizyml` root as an effect of its imports. Its package intentionally lists concrete metrics in `__all__`, and `estimators` and `estimators.lgbm` both list `LGBMAdapter`. For an O4 design with 1-C, give each declared IF one literal `__all__` as its internal named-import declaration. Fail on absence, duplicates, missing bindings, disallowed origins and undeclared consumer imports. Check the origin of each entry against the role table so a stale or newly added concrete export cannot become allowed merely by appearing in the list. Reject whole-module access where the namespace offers a bypass. Six of the eight current Layer 1/2 IF modules have no `__all__`. `features.pipeline_base` and `training.results` already have literal declarations. The former intentionally exports `CategoryStateChange`, so an origin rule must admit declared shared contracts as well as locally defined names. Positive cases should include those two IFs. Negative cases should exercise direct and relative imports, aliased and multi-hop re-exports, stars at both ends, module and parent attributes, an IF leak, and missing, stale and falsely approved entries. Evidence at BLUEPRINT.md:50, lizyml/features/pipeline_base.py:15, lizyml/training/results.py:19, lizyml/metrics/__init__.py:36 and lizyml/estimators/__init__.py:6.

findings.title: Make component freshness depend on an independently checked declaration
findings.detail: The census follows resolvable bases for five nominal interfaces and reports modules. It misses a new class in an already listed module if freshness only compares module names, and it cannot discover all structural providers. `LGBMProvider` has no Protocol base. The current conformance suite enumerates one provider manually, while the Facade selects it lazily and `ModelConfig` has its own discriminator declaration. If O4 is chosen, key the inventory by qualified class and role. Compare it in both directions with an AST census of top-level nominal subclasses under a specified base grammar, including `BaseCalibrationResult`. Require an explicit declaration for structural providers and structural results. Validate provider declarations against the Facade's finite dispatch table, supported Config discriminators and provider conformance test parameters. The current dispatch `if` would need to become a table or another specified finite form for that comparison to be exhaustive. Require an independently enumerable source for declarations, such as a prescribed provider layout with a checked entry in every provider directory and a declared result boundary. Exercise a new nominal class in an existing module, a provider directory without a declaration, an admitted provider missing from the table, a missing concrete result and stale rows. This guarantees freshness for components admitted through those conventions. A class or object that happens to satisfy a Protocol without taking part in an admitted boundary still requires review. Include `CalibrationResult` and `RefitResult`, whose consumer views are `BaseCalibrationResult` and `RefitResultView`. Explicitly classify shared concrete contracts such as `FitResult`, which the loader already checks during migration, and `CategoryStateChange`, which persistence constructs through the IF. For now, keep provider discovery to the declared in-tree providers, including optional providers even when their dependencies are absent. Any future external provider needs explicit Facade admission and conformance checks at the extension boundary. This tree's tests cannot certify external implementation code. Evidence at lizyml/estimators/provider.py:168, lizyml/estimators/lgbm/provider.py:270, lizyml/core/_model_factories.py:493, lizyml/config/schema.py:372, tests/test_estimators/test_check_provider.py:38, lizyml/calibration/cross_fit.py:48, lizyml/training/results.py:22 and lizyml/persistence/loader.py:187.

findings.title: Update the role table from the current tree before pricing O4
findings.detail: The nominal census still reports 13 implementation modules, but `memory_check` now imports `LGBMAdapter` and calls its private `_build_params` in `finalized`. The provider invokes it after checking its own adapter in `resource_warning`, a third concrete adapter check alongside `params_summary` and `build_export_params`. The old four importer groups miss this delegated provider work. If O4 is selected, either give this exact provider helper a narrow role for its own adapter or put the concrete access behind the provider. An annotation-only exemption would still leave the private call to account for. Likewise, declare named Facade roles for construction and concrete-result dispatch, and distinguish the Facade's import of an isotonic constant from permission to construct the calibrator. The constructor probe now reports 254 resolvable calls in Layers 1–3, with 175 in Layer 0, 9 in IF modules, 5 in other-category modules and 65 in same-category modules. Four of the five other-category calls construct the shared `CategoryStateChange` record. A separate AST pass found three nominal implementation constructor calls, the two provider factories and `MASE.bind_train` constructing another `MASE`. The last binds training state after the metric has been selected and belongs outside the assembly rule. The registry-name census moved from 35 to 36 occurrences outside Layer 4 because of the MASE decorator. The dispatch probe moved from 82 to 93 sites, including unresolved and Layer 0 sites. Those counts describe the probe's grammar. Evidence at lizyml/estimators/lgbm/memory_check.py:221, lizyml/estimators/lgbm/provider.py:441, lizyml/estimators/lgbm/provider.py:528, lizyml/estimators/lgbm/provider.py:592, lizyml/core/_model_factories.py:1268, lizyml/core/_model_predict.py:74, lizyml/persistence/_category_preflight.py:204 and lizyml/metrics/regression.py:342.

findings.title: O5 needs a closed write policy as well as a private lookup
findings.detail: Concerns 3 and 4 can be closed for the two shipped registries by construction, with a finite registration schema. Today both instances expose `get`, `keys`, membership, the mutable `_store` and a decorator that overwrites an existing entry. In a standalone stdlib probe, a second registration replaced the first in both objects. Passing `registry.register` into implementations also passes a bound method whose `__self__` is the registry. An underscore on a module-global mapping or lookup function leaves direct attribute access available. Use helper-local storage and export only operations that return a boundary instance or perform validation without returning a class. I recommend the declarative form of O5. Register built-ins at bootstrap from a literal schema of category, key and qualified implementation class, validate unique keys and owned class definitions, and seal the result before publishing the helper functions. A built-in implementation contributes through that schema. There is no importable writer, raw reader, class map or mutable registry instance. If decorators are retained instead, registration must be scoped to the declared owner's class and keys, reject replacement and unauthorized first writes, and end at bootstrap. Duplicate rejection alone allows a caller to claim an unused key. The bound is the two declared built-in registries and their ordinary module and callable surfaces. Extracting closure cells or function globals, patching modules, deriving a class from an instance, or building a separate class table from public exports is outside that bound. Keep review for any new registry or authority change as required by §2.1. Evidence at lizyml/core/registries.py:15, lizyml/core/registries.py:28, lizyml/metrics/registry.py:104, lizyml/calibration/registry.py:19 and BLUEPRINT.md:66.

findings.title: Make the direct-import break and validation migration explicit
findings.detail: O5 breaks direct imports of `MetricRegistry` and `CalibratorRegistry` if the symbols are removed. A partial shim can preserve the import and emit a deprecation diagnostic or expose a safe migration operation, but callers still lose raw `.get`, `.register`, access to `._store`, and any `.keys()` or `in` behavior that the shim omits. A behavior-compatible shim that still returns registered classes or accepts arbitrary registration leaves the corresponding concern open until removal. Prefer an explicit documented break for the two architectural symbols, subject to owner approval in the Proposal. Preserve the metric factories and their task checks, public `get_calibrator`, and public concrete constructors. Replace the Facade's raw `CalibratorRegistry.get(method).validate_params(normalised)` with a validation-only helper that preserves validation before training, normalization, the no-params path, and the distinct LightGBM-backed path. Do not substitute constructor side effects for class validation. Migrate the actual direct-import tests without weakening their population checks. The metric probability test enumerates registered keys, and the two calibration suites check each class's validator, generated fitter parity, and the LightGBM import census. They can use the checked declarations and supported helper operations. Evidence at BLUEPRINT.md:2235, lizyml/core/_model_factories.py:1248, lizyml/calibration/base.py:50, lizyml/calibration/__init__.py:8, tests/test_metrics/test_metric_requires_proba.py:24, tests/test_core/test_calibration_params_reach.py:213 and tests/test_calibration/test_calibration_param_names.py:462.

findings.title: Set explicit bounds for persisted classes and generated programs
findings.detail: O5 can preserve artifact compatibility by keeping persisted classes and their defining paths. The artifact stores the `FitResult` and `RefitResult` objects, their fitted adapters, and the concrete `CalibrationResult` with its `c_final` calibrator. It stores pipeline state in place of pipeline instances. The current exporter writes format 5, and the loader accepts formats 1–5 and unpickles before result migration. Moving the classes to implementation packages would require compatibility at the old defining paths, a remapping loader, or an explicit compatibility break. A package-level re-export or a format bump alone would leave existing references unresolved. The committed calibration pickle names both `calibration.cross_fit.CalibrationResult` and `calibration.platt.PlattCalibrator`. Retain its load test and the old Platt artifact prediction test. For scope item 9, keep selection by name or value that wires an implementation under concern 1. `codegen/generator.py:167`, cited at its former line 140 in the issue, uses `platt` and `beta` to choose a generated dependency. That is a packaging decision under the current definition. Keep generated source outside the in-tree import grammar and retain fitter-key and behavior parity checks, especially when registry keys change. Evidence at lizyml/core/types/fit_result.py:73, lizyml/training/refit_trainer.py:21, lizyml/calibration/cross_fit.py:48, lizyml/persistence/exporter.py:71, lizyml/persistence/loader.py:59, tests/test_architecture/test_h0130_contracts.py:124, tests/test_calibration/test_i298_pr3c_evidence.py:369 and HISTORY.md:14215.

findings.title: Choose O5 only and stop review at a fixed acceptance matrix
findings.detail: Rank 1 is O5 only, medium, with the two architectural-symbol breaks and tests for concerns 3 and 4 within the built-in registry boundary. Concerns 1 and 2 stay under review. Loop risk is low once registration and compatibility are fixed. Rank 2 is to close #366 with a documented review-only bound, small, with zero runtime compatibility cost and all four concerns still reviewed. This is the fallback if the owner chooses to preserve the raw symbols. It needs an explicit update to the current merge-based end condition. Rank 3 is O5 plus O4, medium to large, with O5's break and internal import refactoring. It adds a bounded acquisition test for parts of 1 and 2, which both still need review. Loop risk rises with export and inventory coverage. Rank 4 is O5 plus O4 plus full 1-C, large, with the same enforcement split and additional IF declarations and import restrictions. A runtime export cleanup would also affect clients of incidental IF names. Its review surface is the broadest. Rank 5 is O4 plus 1-C alone, medium to large, with the same import-boundary cost and all four semantic concerns still under review. It adds the bounded acquisition check while leaving both global registries reachable. For rank 1, fix acceptance before drafting implementation. For each of the two registries, test that the old raw handle and its IF or package aliases are absent, the helpers expose no raw class map or writer, schema duplicates and unauthorized entries fail, and each declared key constructs through its helper. Exercise unknown names, bad parameters, metric task compatibility, calibration preflight, import order, public constructors and the old artifact fixture. Verify that the migrated tests still iterate the full registered population. Confirm that disabling either the capability boundary or schema validation makes its corresponding test fail. End the amendment's temporary treatment when that implementation and matching tests merge. Update BLUEPRINT, the PR template and the architecture summaries to leave 1 and 2 under review and record the explicit bounds of 3 and 4. Review stops at the published schema, capability, compatibility and test criteria. Another spelling of an explicitly excluded operation supplies no new acceptance criterion. Evidence at BLUEPRINT.md:69, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:9 and HISTORY.md:14278.

findings.title: Verification was limited to read-only probes
findings.detail: The stdlib checker returned zero problems on the unmodified tree and scanned 595 edges across 151 source modules. I ran the import, registry-name, constructor and dispatch censuses, the in-memory R0–R5 mutations, and the standalone registry and pickle-opcode probes. The runtime boundary constructor census stopped at the missing generated `lizyml._version`. The pytest suite and H-0130 pytest negative controls could not run because pytest is absent. NumPy, pandas, LightGBM, Optuna and joblib are also absent, so I did not execute package initialization, training, or artifact load and prediction. The digest identifies the supplied tree, which has no usable Git HEAD for independent verification. Evidence at lizyml/__init__.py:3 and docs/audits/2026-10-h0130/probes/negative_controls_h0130.py:18.
